title: Sparse Hamiltonian simulation with optimal dependence on the maximum column Euclidean norm
abstract: We give a quantum algorithm for simulating a $d$-sparse Hermitian Hamiltonian $H$, assuming a known upper bound $Λ$ on its maximum column Euclidean norm $\|H\|_{1\to2}$. For $tΛ\ge1/2$, simulation with operator-norm error $ε$ uses \[   O\!\left(tΛ\sqrt d+\sqrt d\log(2/ε)\right) \] sparse-oracle queries. This removes the subpolynomial overhead in Low's algorithm [STOC 2019], replacing it with an additive logarithmic precision term. For $d>1$ and $tΛ\ge\log(2/ε)$, the bound matches the worst-case lower bound. A known spectral-norm upper bound may also be used in place of $Λ$. The number of 1- and 2-qubit gates is linear in the query scale, up to oracle costs and polynomial overhead in the input bit lengths and logarithmic precision parameters.   As applications, we obtain $O(κ\sqrt d\,\mathrm{polylog}(κ/ε))$ queries for solving $d$-sparse quantum linear systems with $\|A\|\le1$ and $\|A^{-1}\|\leκ$, under standard sparse and state-preparation access. We also give a gate-efficient implementation of black-box unitaries with at most $d$ nonzero entries per row and column using $O(\sqrt d\log(2/ε))$ queries, given sparse access to the unitary and its adjoint. At constant error, the query bound is optimal and yields $Θ(\sqrt N)$ queries for arbitrary $N\times N$ unitaries, resolving the open question on black-box unitary implementation posed by Berry and Childs [QIC 2012].
summary: This paper presents advanced quantum algorithms for simulating time evolution generated by sparse Hamiltonians and implementing sparse unitaries. By optimizing the dependence on the Hamiltonian's norm and sparsity, the authors achieve query complexities that match theoretical lower bounds. This work significantly advances the practical feasibility of quantum simulation for complex physical systems.
main_problem: Developing quantum algorithms to simulate sparse Hermitian Hamiltonians and implement general sparse unitaries with optimal query complexity.
main_result: The authors achieve query complexities for Hamiltonian simulation and unitary implementation that remove subpolynomial overheads, matching known lower bounds for certain tasks.
method: The work employs sparse-access quantum oracles and sophisticated circuit constructions, including forward reuse techniques, to approximate time evolution and unitaries.
model_or_system: The focus is on simulating quantum systems governed by a $d$-sparse Hermitian Hamiltonian $H$ (i.e., $e^{-itH}$), and implementing general $d$-row-sparse unitaries $U$.
key_observables: Operator-norm error ($\epsilon$), number of sparse-oracle queries, and gate counts.
important_parameters: Sparsity parameter ($d$), maximum column Euclidean norm bound ($\Lambda$), evolution time ($t$), and desired precision ($\epsilon$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes access to sparse-access oracles for the Hamiltonian or unitary, and the complexity analysis relies on bounding error accumulation through structured circuit constructions.
paper_structure: The paper builds from the core simulation problem (Theorem 1) to specific applications like solving sparse linear systems and implementing unitaries. Subsequent analysis details the underlying circuit techniques (forward reuse, isometry construction) to prove the optimal query bounds.
why_interesting: The results provide concrete, near-optimal quantum computational resources for simulating physical Hamiltonians, which is crucial for designing quantum algorithms for quantum chemistry or condensed matter simulations.
